name: Eritrea
tagline: Art deco Asmara, and the Dahlak islands
summary: A modernist capital on a highland plateau that UNESCO listed whole, a steam railway down to the Red Sea, and three hundred islands off Massawa that almost nobody visits.
when: October to April. Asmara is temperate all year; the coast is only bearable in winter.

entries.caption: Asmara on the Plateau
entries.description: A whole modernist city at 2,300 metres, built in the 1930s and barely altered since.
entries.subject: the Fiat Tagliero building in Asmara with its concrete wings

entries.caption: The Escarpment
entries.description: The plateau drops two thousand metres to the Red Sea in about ninety kilometres.
entries.subject: the Eritrean highland escarpment dropping away in terraces

entries.caption: Danakil and Dahlak
entries.description: Wild ass in the Danakil, dugong and turtle in the Dahlak archipelago.
entries.subject: an African wild ass on stony ground in the Danakil

entries.caption: Not the Business Here
entries.description: There is no safari circuit. The wildlife is coastal and marine, and it is worth the swap.
entries.subject: a green turtle over seagrass in the Dahlak archipelago

entries.caption: Emba Soira
entries.description: 3,018 metres in the southern highlands, with terraced farming right up the sides.
entries.subject: terraced fields climbing the slopes of the Eritrean highlands

entries.caption: Seasonal Only
entries.description: The highland streams run in the summer rains and are dry the rest of the year.
entries.subject: a dry rocky streambed in the Eritrean highlands

entries.caption: The Red Sea Coast
entries.description: No permanent rivers to speak of — the water here is the sea, and it is very warm.
entries.subject: clear shallow water over coral off the Eritrean Red Sea coast

entries.caption: The Dahlak Archipelago
entries.description: Three hundred and fifty islands, four of them inhabited, and reefs almost nobody has dived.
entries.subject: an empty white beach and turquoise water on a Dahlak island

entries.caption: The Green Belt
entries.description: Semenawi Bahri, a strip of cloud forest on the escarpment an hour from the capital.
entries.subject: mist in the cloud forest of Semenawi Bahri on the escarpment

entries.caption: The Massawa Road
entries.description: Down the escarpment by road or by the restored steam railway, two thousand metres in a morning.
entries.subject: a steam locomotive on the mountain railway above Asmara

entries.caption: Nine Groups, Two Faiths
entries.description: Tigrinya, Tigre, Afar, Bilen and five more, roughly half Christian and half Muslim.
entries.subject: people at an outdoor cafe on Harnet Avenue in Asmara

entries.caption: The Afar and the Rashaida
entries.description: The Afar on the southern coast, and the Rashaida who came across from Arabia in the 1840s.
entries.subject: a Rashaida woman in an embroidered veil near the Red Sea coast

entries.caption: Injera, Zigni and Macchiato
entries.description: Eritrean stews on injera, and an Italian coffee culture that never left.
entries.subject: a macchiato in a glass on a marble cafe table in Asmara

entries.caption: Meskel and Eid
entries.description: Meskel bonfires in September, and Eid in Massawa, in the same country and often the same street.
entries.subject: a Meskel bonfire and crowd in an Eritrean town square

entries.caption: Filigree and Basketry
entries.description: Silver filigree from Asmara's goldsmiths, and coiled straw baskets from the highlands.
entries.subject: silver filigree jewellery on a workbench in Asmara

entries.caption: Adulis and Qohaito
entries.description: A Red Sea port that traded with Rome, and a highland city on the escarpment above it.
entries.subject: stone columns standing at the ruins of Qohaito on the escarpment

entries.caption: Asmara, Listed Whole
entries.description: The first modernist city anywhere to be inscribed as a World Heritage site, in 2017.
entries.subject: the modernist facade of the Cinema Impero on Harnet Avenue

entries.caption: Asmara and Massawa
entries.description: One a cool art-deco plateau town, the other a coral-block Ottoman port on the sea.
entries.subject: coral-block Ottoman buildings on the waterfront at Massawa

entries.caption: Futurist and Coral
entries.description: Fiat Tagliero's concrete wings in Asmara, and Massawa's buildings cut from the reef itself.
entries.subject: the arched coral-stone facade of an old Massawa merchant house

entries.caption: The Passeggiata
entries.description: Asmara walks Harnet Avenue in the evening. Everybody does, and nobody hurries.
entries.subject: people walking Harnet Avenue in Asmara in the evening

entries.caption: The Safest Capital Around
entries.description: Asmara is small, walkable and calm, and children are everywhere in it after dark.
entries.subject: children playing in a public square in Asmara at dusk

entries.caption: Cycling
entries.description: Eritrea is a cycling country — the Tour of Eritrea climbs the escarpment.
entries.subject: a peloton of cyclists climbing a mountain road in Eritrea

entries.caption: Modest, and Improving
entries.description: A handful of restored Italian-era hotels in Asmara. Nothing on the coast yet.
entries.subject: a restored Italian-era hotel interior in Asmara

entries.caption: Terraces That Hold the Soil
entries.description: Highland terracing built by hand over centuries, and still the reason the topsoil is there.
entries.subject: hand-built stone terraces on a steep Eritrean hillside

entries.caption: Deco in Low Light
entries.description: Asmara's facades in the late afternoon, when the plaster goes warm and the streets empty.
entries.subject: late sun on a curved art deco facade in Asmara

entries.caption: The Tank Graveyard
entries.description: A hillside outside Asmara stacked with the wreckage of thirty years of war.
entries.subject: rusting tanks and vehicles stacked at the Asmara tank graveyard

entries.caption: Why Eritrea
entries.description: Nowhere else has a whole intact modernist city, a steam railway and an unfished reef.
entries.subject: a vintage Fiat parked outside an art deco cinema in Asmara
